title: Guard-Checking Machine from Ready Tapes
statement: For every machine format $F$, every $k\\ge4$, there exist a finite state set $S$, a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and states $S$, an entry state, an injective map from the Boolean values to states, and a constant $a\\in\\mathbb N$. For all Boolean words $x,bits,rest$ parsed from $x$ as $(bits,rest)$, the machine, started on $x$ with the prescribed ready words on its tapes, reaches within $t\\le a(|x|+1)$ steps the exit state indexed by whether $B_F(\\operatorname{val}(bits)+1)\\le |rest|$, where $B_F=\\max(\\operatorname{guard}(F),(4k+5)3^{k+1})$; at that time its output is empty, its input-head position is $2|bits|+3$ when the inequality holds and $|x|+1$ otherwise, and every tape except tape $1$ retains its prescribed ready word with its head at zero. No earlier time is in either exit state.
hypotheses_covered: finite state set $S$ and decidable equality

initial configuration uses the prescribed ready words
